# Non-Occupational:

# Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (nPEP) for Exposure to Blood or Body Fluids

# Treatment recommendations:

All persons offered nPEP should be prescribed a 28-30 day course of a 3-drug antiretroviral regimen.

* IMPORTANT- First dose should be given as soon as possible after exposure
* These medications may be taken with or without food
* Side effects of these medications are infrequent but may include:

nausea, vomiting, diarrha, rash, fever, headaches, insomnia, arthralgias, fatigue, abdominal pain, hepatitis, renal dysfunction, rare lactic acidosis

# Select appropriate treatment below based on patient renal function:

# Creatinine clearance >/= 15 ml/min:

[Biktarvy 50/200/25 TAB 1 PO qday for 30 days R,DI](psozid-biktarvy-1-po-qday-x30days)

[Biktarvy combination tab-bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide]

# Creatinine clearance < 15 ml/min not on dialysis*:

[Emtricitabine 200MG/Tenofovir 300MG Tab 1 po q3days R,DI < AND >](orz-set-abx-op-pep-non-occup-dolutegravir-truvada-crcl-30)

Dolutegravir 50MG Tab 1 po qday [DI] for 28 days

*Recommend close ID follow up within 1-2 weeks.

# ESRD dialysis:

[Biktarvy 50/200/25 TAB 1 PO qday for 30 days R,DI](psozid-biktarvy-1-po-qday-x30days)

[Biktarvy combination tab-bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide]

Note: All of the above listed medications are recommended for treatment and prevention of HIV during pregnancy.

References:

- CDC Guidelines 2025
